page: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 96 dedicated physical cores running on 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation without hyperthreading, supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a 128 MB L3 cache pool. The platform includes 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 5669 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing scalability alongside average single-threaded output. In multi-core assessments, the instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 845.64 GB/sec, and Geekbench multi-core workloads, including Clang compilation and ray tracing. Conversely, single-core benchmarks such as single-core stress-ng and Geekbench single-core operate within median ranges. Memory subsystem testing reflects top-tier read bandwidth reaching 464.56 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 205.51 GB/sec on large uncached blocks.

The 2.0 GB per core memory footprint establishes this instance as a compute-dense configuration rather than a balanced general-purpose allocation. This architecture prioritizes parallel compute capacity and fast local NVMe storage over expansive memory reserves. High uncached memory throughput and 5669 GB of rapid NVMe storage deliver balanced efficiency for data operations, as demonstrated by PassMark database operations and Redis throughput reaching 170.06 million SET operations per second.

Microsoft Azure D96plds_v6 is suited for multi-threaded compilation, batch data processing, distributed caching, web serving arrays, and intermediate database workloads that require high parallel core counts and fast local disk scratch space without requiring substantial memory allocation per thread.
description: Microsoft Azure D96plds_v6 is an ARM-powered cloud server configured with 96 dedicated physical cores running on 3.4 GHz Microsoft ARM Neoverse-N2 processors without hyperthreading. The instance includes 192.0 GB of RAM, yielding a lean 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, paired with 5669 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and no integrated GPUs. Synthetic and real-world benchmarks show top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, evidenced by strong scores in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench Clang compilation, and high-frequency Redis operations exceeding 170 million operations per second. However, single-core performance remains in the middle tier. Given its high core density, rapid uncached memory throughput, and extensive local disk capacity, the D96plds_v6 provides an efficient platform for large-scale multi-threaded compilation, high-concurrency web serving, and database workloads requiring high parallel throughput rather than massive memory-per-core allocations.
